business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 business description
business_model.claim: Boston Beer makes and sells alcohol beverages: flavored malt beverages (Twisted Tea), hard seltzer (Truly), beer (Samuel Adams, Dogfish Head), hard cider (Angry Orchard), spirits RTDs (Sun Cruiser) and some distilled spirits. It brews at its own breweries and cidery and under contract at other producers' facilities.
quotes: The Company produces alcohol beverages, including flavored malt beverages, hard seltzer, beer, hard cider, spirits based ready to drink beverages

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A
business_model.claim: Customers are mainly independent distributors, not drinkers. The company sells to a network of over 300 wholesalers, who sell on to retailers such as grocery, club, convenience and liquor stores, bars and restaurants. The largest distributor was about 3% of gross sales and the top three about 7%, so distributor concentration is low.
quotes: the Company sells most of its alcohol beverages to independent beer Distributors for distribution to retailers and, ultimately, to drinkers
During 2025, the Company’s largest individual Distributor accounted for approximately 3% of the Company’s gross sales.

business_model.basis: stated in the 10-K Item 1 and Item 1A
business_model.claim: The business is mostly in the United States, where approximately 94% of beverages are sold. About 86% of 2025 volume was in Beyond beer, with the rest in Traditional beer, and the company ranks second in Beyond beer with a 20% share.
quotes: In 2025, approximately 86% of the Company’s volume is in Beyond beer with the remainder in Traditional beer.

business_model.claim: Category trends set the demand backdrop. In 2025 the flavored malt beverage category declined 4% and hard seltzer declined 4.5%, while spirits RTDs grew approximately 29%. The company's largest brands sit in the declining categories, and Sun Cruiser sits in the growing one.
quotes: Since 2021, the category has seen significant declines in volume.

business_model.basis: inferred from the one-reporting-unit statement and the description of shared customers and channels; no segment note is in the evidence
business_model.claim: The company reports one reporting unit for goodwill, and its beverages are sold to the same types of customers through substantially the same channels with similar production processes. The excerpts give no separate segment table, so this points to a single business, but I am inferring that.
quotes: The Company has one reporting unit.

The Company’s beverages are sold by the Company’s sales force to the same types of customers and drinkers in similar size quantities, at similar price points and through substantially the same channels of distribution.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement (table in thousands)
business_model.claim: Net revenue is gross revenue less excise taxes. In the nine months to Sep. 26, 2026, revenue of 1,624,792 less excise taxes of 102,423 left net revenue of 1,522,369 (all figures in thousands of USD).

business_model.basis: stated in 10-Q MD&A, with the price guidance in the earnings release
business_model.claim: Revenue moves with volume, price and product mix. In Q3 2026, net revenue fell $17.4 million, or 3.2%, to $520.1 million. A volume effect of $26.4 million was partly offset by favorable mix of $7.7 million and pricing of $4.9 million.
quotes: Net revenue decreased by $17.4 million, or 3.2%, to $520.1 million for the thirteen weeks ended September 26, 2026

business_model.claim: Volume is the main swing factor and is falling. Q3 shipments fell 4.9% to 1,841,000 barrels, driven by Twisted Tea, Truly, Samuel Adams and Hard Mountain Dew, partly offset by Sun Cruiser and Angry Orchard. The company says demand remains challenging.
quotes: The decrease was primarily driven by decreases in Twisted Tea, Truly, Samuel Adams and Hard Mountain Dew brands that were partially offset by increases in Sun Cruiser and Angry Orchard brands.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-Q MD&A and the earnings release
business_model.claim: Cost of goods per barrel is held roughly flat by cost savings offsetting inflation. In Q3 it was $136.35 per barrel against $136.56. Inflation of $10.2 million, mainly aluminum, was offset by savings from contract renegotiations, brewery efficiencies and lower third-party production payment amortization. Gross margin was 51.7%.
quotes: Inflationary impacts of $10.2 million consist primarily of increased material costs, mainly from aluminum, of $7.6 million, inclusive of $0.8 million impact from tariffs, and increased internal brewery costs of $0.5 million.

business_model.claim: Production is increasingly in company-owned breweries, which makes costs more fixed. Own breweries made 86% of domestic volume in 2025, up from 74% in 2024, and the company expects over 90% in 2026. About 14% was still made at City Brewing in 2025.
quotes: The Company has increased the percentage of its domestic volume produced at Company owned breweries from 74% in 2024 to 86% in 2025 and is currently estimating a further increase to over 90% in 2026.

business_model.basis: stated in 10-Q MD&A and the income statement
business_model.claim: Advertising, promotional and selling expense is the largest operating cost and includes freight. It was flat at $165 million in Q3, at 31.8% of net revenue. Higher freight of $9.5 million was offset by a $9.0 million cut in advertising.
quotes: The Company includes freight charges related to the movement of finished goods from its manufacturing locations to distributor locations in its advertising, promotional and selling expense line item.
